synopsis: The booklet presents software interfaces and programming environments as practical integration choices: CARLA offers Python, Prescan offers Python and MATLAB, RoadRunner uses gRPC, and ROS 2 is integrated across several simulators [f16237, f16240]. Version instability is a central planning risk: CARLA changed from UE4 to UE5 with some APIs unsupported, while Isaac Sim 5.0 deprecated camera-prim RTX workflows and removed annotators; evidence may therefore need re-qualification after updates [f8892, f8487, f16247]. Recommended controls are to freeze and containerize the tool chain, archive containers for the safety case, regression-test upgrades, and record the software build or commit in every run [f16241, f16248, f16243]. Open-source delivery avoids license lock-in but brings GPU, library and version dependencies, requiring reproducible builds, internal competence, upstream and security-patch tracking, and DevOps labor [f8898, f8900, f16244]. Acquisition planning should include cloud and continuous-integration skills, partner handover of continuous-integration scripts, and a software bill of materials with asset and license review for mixed licensing [f16245, f16246, f8909].
